newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay index closes 4.4 pct higher in hectic trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay index closes 4.4 pct higher in hectic trade.

text.p: Bombay stocks staged a powerful rally on Wednesday, as buying euphoria helped the benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index soar 4.4 percent, its biggest gain in the New Year, dealers said.
"The market was on fire...there's a lot of speculation going on," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at Kotak Securities, a domestic brokerage.
"Bull operators are trying to make a killing..."
Participants said aggressive bidding by local speculators and mounting optimism about likely government announcements drove the market higher.

"There appears to be a spillover of the excess liquidity in the domestic economy into the stock market. The key driver for that is the higher level of expectations on the government policy front," said Rajashekar Iyer, research head at Kotak Securities, the Indian affiliate of Goldman Sachs.
"There is more risk of the market being disappointed by government policy now," Iyer said.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda earlier this month said the government was working on policies to pep up industrial growth and dormant capital markets.
No details have yet been announced.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram is expected to present the 1997/98 (April-March) budget to parliament in on February 28.
On Wednesday, the top 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) vaulted 153.47 points, or 4.4 percent, to end at a provisional 3,645.73, off the day's high of 3,673.91.
ACC surged 127.70 rupees to 1,599.0 rupees, SBI 24.75 to 291.25, ITC 35.50 to 416.50, L&T 13.25 to 263.0, Reliance 16.75 to 254.50 and TISCO 11.25 to 205.50.
The National Stock Exchange index jumped 51.50 points or 5.21 percent to 1,040.80 on the first day of weekly account.
